title: Coherent formal modules with support proper over the base form Serre subcategories
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, $f:X\to S$ a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (so $X$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Each of the following full subcategories $\mathcal C$ of the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] is a Serre subcategory, i.e. contains $0$ and, for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C'\to0$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal B\in\mathcal C$ if and only if $\mathcal A\in\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal C'\in\mathcal C$: (1) $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$, the objects $(\mathcal F_n)$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_1)$ proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]; (2) the objects $(\mathcal F_n)$ for which there is a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z\to S$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n\ge1$, $\mathcal I_Z$ the ideal sheaf of $Z$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] (that is, $(\mathcal F_n)$ is supported on $Z$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (3)).

proof.text: (Supports in a short exact sequence.) $X$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is an abelian category. Three facts on stalks of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $\operatorname{Supp}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2): (i) if $\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal Q$ is a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module then $\mathcal P_x\to\mathcal Q_x$ is injective (a germ $s_x$, $s\in\mathcal P(U)$, that vanishes in $\mathcal Q_x$ has $s|_W=0$ in $\mathcal Q(W)\supseteq\mathcal P(W)$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq U$), so $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal P\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal Q$; (ii) if $\mathcal Q\to\mathcal R$ is surjective then $\mathcal Q_x\to\mathcal R_x$ is surjective, since every section of $\mathcal R$ lifts on a neighbourhood of $x$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1); so $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal R\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal Q$; (iii) if $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ is exact at $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal A_x=0=\mathcal C_x$, then $\mathcal B_x=0$: for $s\in\mathcal B(U)$ the image of $s$ in $\mathcal C$ has zero germ, hence vanishes on an open $x\in W\subseteq U$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (2) $s|_{W'}$ is the image of a section $t$ of $\mathcal A$ on some open $x\in W'\subseteq W$, and $s_x$ is the image of $t_x=0$. Now let $0\to(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)\xrightarrow{\alpha}(\mathcal H_n)\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-short-exact-levels] (a) for $n=1$, $\mathcal G_1\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal H_1\to0$ is exact, so $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H_1\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1$ by (ii) and $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G_1\cup\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H_1$ by (iii). By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-short-exact-levels] (b) for $n=1$ there are $m\ge1$ and a surjection $\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_m)\to\mathcal G_1$, so by (ii), (i) and [lem-weil-pbc-formal-system-support-constant], $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G_1\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_m)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_m=\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1$. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1=\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G_1\cup\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H_1$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), proof, remarks (a), (b) and the proof of (1): Supp(F_n) = Supp(F_1) and Supp(G_1) cup Supp(H_1) = Supp(F_1); the stalk facts (i)-(iii) are written out by the agent

proof.text: (The supports are closed.) $X$ is locally Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so for every object $(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ the coherent module $\mathcal F_1$ is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] and $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1$ is a closed subset of $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. As $f$ is of finite type, in particular locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], 'proper over $S$' is defined for closed subsets of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), proof; closedness of supports as in Lemma 0CYU (lemma-cat-module-support-proper-over-base) via Morphisms Lemma 056J

proof.text: (The empty set.) The empty closed subscheme $E=\emptyset$ of $X$ (the closed immersion $\emptyset\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], with ideal sheaf $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to0)=\mathcal O_X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]) is proper over $S$: the morphism $\emptyset\to S$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $\emptyset$ and $\mathcal O_S\to0$ is surjective, so it is a closed immersion, hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c). The empty scheme is reduced and is the reduced induced closed subscheme structure on the closed subset $\emptyset$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (1), so the closed subset $\emptyset\subseteq X$ is proper over $S$.

proof.text: (Proof of (1).) Let $\mathcal C_1$ be the subcategory (1). The zero object $(0)_n$ has $\operatorname{Supp}(0)=\emptyset$, proper over $S$ by Step 3, so $(0)_n\in\mathcal C_1$. Let $0\to(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal H_n)\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$; by Step 1, $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1=\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G_1\cup\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H_1$, all three closed by Step 2. If $(\mathcal F_n)\in\mathcal C_1$, the closed subsets $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G_1,\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H_1\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1$ are proper over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (2). If $(\mathcal G_n),(\mathcal H_n)\in\mathcal C_1$, their union $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_1$ is proper over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-union-preimage] (1). So $\mathcal C_1$ is a Serre subcategory in the sense of the statement.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), proof of (1), with Lemma 0CYN (lemma-closed-closed-proper-over-base) and Lemma 0CYR (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base)

proof.text: (Annihilators.) For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal P$, $\mathcal J\mathcal P$ is the image of $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal P\to\mathcal P$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0); the tensor product is the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal J(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal P(U)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], so each of its sections is locally a finite sum of tensors $a\otimes s$, and $\mathcal J\mathcal P=0$ if and only if $as=0$ for all opens $U$, $a\in\mathcal J(U)$, $s\in\mathcal P(U)$. Hence: (i) if $\mathcal J\mathcal Q=0$ and $\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal Q$ then $\mathcal J\mathcal P=0$; (ii) if $\mathcal J\mathcal Q=0$ and $\mathcal Q\to\mathcal R$ is surjective then $\mathcal J\mathcal R=0$ (for $r\in\mathcal R(U)$, $a\in\mathcal J(U)$, locally $r$ is the image of some $q$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1), so $ar$ is locally the image of $aq=0$, and $ar=0$ by the sheaf property); (iii) if $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ is exact at $\mathcal B$, $\mathcal J'\mathcal A=0$ and $\mathcal J\mathcal C=0$, then $(\mathcal J'\mathcal J)\mathcal B=0$ for the product ideal [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]: for $b\in\mathcal B(U)$, $a\in\mathcal J(U)$, $a'\in\mathcal J'(U)$ the image of $ab$ in $\mathcal C$ is $a$ times the image of $b$, i.e. $0$, so on an open covering $U=\bigcup U_i$, $ab|_{U_i}$ is the image of some $t_i\in\mathcal A(U_i)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (2), and $a'ab|_{U_i}$ is the image of $a't_i=0$; thus $a'ab=0$, and since the sections of $\mathcal J'\mathcal J$ (the image of $\mathcal J'\otimes\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_X$) are locally finite sums of products $a'a$, $(\mathcal J'\mathcal J)\mathcal B=0$.

proof.text: (Proof of (2): zero object, subobjects and quotients.) Let $\mathcal C_2$ be the subcategory (2). The empty closed subscheme $E$ of Step 3 is proper over $S$ and $\mathcal I_E\cdot0=0$, so $(0)_n\in\mathcal C_2$. Let $0\to(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)\xrightarrow{\alpha}(\mathcal H_n)\to0$ be short exact in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ and $Z\subseteq X$ a closed subscheme with $Z\to S$ proper and $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-short-exact-levels] (a), $\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal H_n$ is surjective, so $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal H_n=0$ (Step 5 (ii)). By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-short-exact-levels] (b), for each $n$ there are $m\ge n$ and a surjection $\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_m)\to\mathcal G_n$; as $\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_m)\subseteq\mathcal F_m$, $\mathcal I_Z\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_m)=0$ (Step 5 (i)) and $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal G_n=0$ (Step 5 (ii)). So $(\mathcal G_n),(\mathcal H_n)\in\mathcal C_2$, with the same $Z$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), proof of (2), first part

proof.text: (Proof of (2): extensions.) In the situation of Step 6 suppose instead that $Z,Y\subseteq X$ are closed subschemes with $Z\to S$, $Y\to S$ proper, $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal G_n=0$ and $\mathcal I_Y\mathcal H_n=0$ for all $n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-short-exact-levels] (a) and Step 5 (iii) (with $\mathcal J'=\mathcal I_Z$, $\mathcal J=\mathcal I_Y$), $(\mathcal I_Z\mathcal I_Y)\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-product-ideal-closed-subscheme-union] there is a closed subscheme $W\subseteq X$ with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_W=\mathcal I_Z\mathcal I_Y$ and underlying set $Z\cup Y$. The closed subsets $Z$, $Y$ are proper over $S$, since they carry a closed subscheme structure proper over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (1); so $Z\cup Y$ is proper over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-union-preimage] (1), and therefore $W\to S$ is proper, $W$ being a closed subscheme structure on $Z\cup Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (1). Thus $(\mathcal F_n)\in\mathcal C_2$. With Step 6, $\mathcal C_2$ is a Serre subcategory in the sense of the statement.

lean.statement: theorem formalSystems_properSupport_serre {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (I : X.IdealSheafData) : Nonempty (Abelian (@CoherentFormalModule X (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f) I)) ∧ ∀ [Ab : Abelian (@CoherentFormalModule X (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f) I)], ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass (fun M : @CoherentFormalModule X (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f) I ↦ Scheme.Modules.HasSupportProperOver f (M.obj.obj (op 0))) ∧ ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass (fun M : @CoherentFormalModule X (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f) I ↦ ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i), IsProper (i ≫ f) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct i.ker.toModulesι (M.obj.obj (op n))))
